correctness.rationale: The two products list the same nonempty cells; their row-first and column-first orders differ exactly when a pair of cells has reversed row and column indices. Thus each commuting partition is an arbitrary ordered partition inside each A_i, with the consecutive restrictions joined or kept separate independently at each interface. This yields the claimed factor and the multinomial composition multiplicities. The representation F_m = (1/2)∑_{r≥0} r^m/2^r gives strict log-convexity by Cauchy–Schwarz (the powers are not proportional on the positive support). Moving a unit from a larger part to a part at least two smaller lowers the product, and moving a unit from a part greater than one to a part at least as large raises it. This proves the precise balanced and concentrated equality cases, including trivial boundary compositions. The block generating function is T=(e^z−1)/(2−e^z), giving 1+T/(1−2T) and the Stirling expansion. The unique closest poles are log 2 and log(4/3), with residues −1/2 and −1/12 for the ordered Bell and commuting-pair series; taking the ratio of coefficients with the factorials gives the stated probability. The supplied Python checker is consistent with testing all pairs through n=5, not a proof of the asymptotic or extrema.
residual_risks: The recorded checker was inspected, not executed; the general results were verified by reconstructing the mathematical argument.
